title: What If Earth Froze Over Like Snowball Earth?

scenes.text: What if Earth froze solid? It already did, and it stayed frozen for millions of years.
Between about 720 and 635 million years ago, geologists find two great ice ages: the Sturtian and the Marinoan.
Buried in massive ice sheets, surface temperatures fell as low as minus fifty degrees Celsius.
It lasted tens of millions of years, because frozen land blocked the weathering that normally removes carbon dioxide.
Meanwhile, volcanoes kept erupting beneath the ice, pumping carbon dioxide into the air for millions of years.
Eventually that gas warmed the planet enough to melt the ice cover quickly, ending the deepest freeze Earth has known.
